prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and the identity of its active form, which made incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-part B035 prize for Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The round-1 exchange tested the case and it held. All six members regard the chain from proglucagon processing through the truncated active peptide and receptor biology to drugs confirmed in large independent outcome trials as complete and mature, and nobody raised a maturity objection. The dispute is about attribution and framing, not merit. I settle the third seat for Mojsov because a Physiology or Medicine citation is best anchored on what was discovered about how the incretin system works, and the identification of the active form of the peptide is a discovery step. The citation I propose names the physiology and the active form, and says that these made the therapy possible, so the drug-development leg is acknowledged without the prize being written as a prize for a product.
statement.case_against: The weakest point is still the third seat. Mojsov's priority for GLP-1(7-36) is publicly contested, Habener-type work lies outside the credited names, and none of us can resolve the priority record from the supplied material, which is the only evidence I am allowed to rely on here. Omitting Knudsen, whose long-acting analogues turned the hormone into a drug, leaves a real fairness question and risks the reading that the committee honoured the idea and not the medicine. A trio with Mojsov may draw an attribution dispute, and a trio with Knudsen may be criticised for rewarding industrial development over discovery. I also accept that a single-part prize leaves UPR (B047), CAR-T (B014) and SMN2 antisense (B028) for later years, which I am prepared to do because the three-person cap makes a second part impossible without removing a B035 name.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius keeps Knudsen in the third seat with a citation that runs from GLP-1 physiology to long-acting incretin therapies, arguing that the three names should span physiology, receptor biology and translation.
responses.response: This is the strongest alternative to my trio, and the question it forces is what the prize is for. I considered it again. My difficulty is that a Knudsen trio makes the prize rest on the engineering of albumin-binding analogues, which is industrial development shared across a team, while leaving the identity of the active peptide, which is the physiological discovery, uncredited. Drucker and Holst already carry the receptor biology and the human physiology, so the third seat is the only place where the active-form discovery can be credited. I do not change my position, but I took one point from your statement: the citation should say that the discoveries made the therapies possible, so the clinical consequence is explicit. If the committee decides that development must be named, a Knudsen trio is a defensible fallback and I would not call it unfair. I would only insist that the citation then states plainly why a development contribution is being honoured.

responses.point: Linnarsson holds the Mojsov trio but says that if the attribution problems cannot be resolved, a cleaner candidate such as B028 with a compact two-person credit becomes more attractive.
responses.response: I follow the logic but I do not think the attribution problem at the third seat is large enough to demote the strongest scientific case. Drucker and Holst are named by all six of us, and the uncertainty concerns one seat. B028 has its own gaps, since the discovery of the SMN2 target site by other groups and the SMN1 gene identification are outside the credited pair, and its platform consequences are still unfolding. Switching to it would trade a contested seat for a less mature case and would not remove attribution questions. I would keep B028 as a strong later-year candidate, and I read your concern as a reason to be careful with the citation wording.

responses.point: Sandberg describes Holst as human physiology and secretion, Drucker as receptor biology and gut-pancreas actions, and Mojsov as identification and synthesis of the active form, and notes that this trio is the wrong one if the committee intends to honour the drugs themselves.
responses.response: I agree with that division of roles and it is the clearest way I have seen it put, because it shows why each of the three names a different step in the discovery. Your closing caveat is also right, and it is the crux of what the chair's questions asked. I think the committee should decide this explicitly. My answer is that the committee should prize the discovery side, and I would not describe the choice as settled by the unanimity on the first-place ranking. On Habener-type contributions, I see no way to repair the omission within three seats. I treat it as a limit that applies to every trio, and it does not discriminate between Mojsov and Knudsen, so it should not drive the choice.

responses.point: Perlmann prefers a single-achievement prize attached to a discovery and not to a product, and keeps B011 and B014 as possible second parts for a later round given their upstream credit problems.
responses.response: I agree on a single-achievement prize and I share your reading that B011 and B014 are held back by credit upstream of their named trios. I would add that the three-person limit decides the question for this year regardless of how strong the second candidate is: any second part would require removing a B035 laureate, and all six of us name Drucker and Holst while five name Mojsov. I am therefore not proposing a second part. Your earlier point on dopamine-neuron colleagues is noted for the conflict disclosure below, and it does not touch any credited name.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov or Knudsen should hold the third GLP-1 seat. I cannot verify the priority record for the active peptide from the supplied material and my account of the incretin history is general recollection.
Whether a physiology-led citation can be worded so that it is fair to both a Mojsov trio and a Knudsen trio. I have tried to acknowledge the therapy explicitly without naming drug design.
How much the absence of Habener-type contributions should count against any B035 trio; I judge that it applies to every configuration and does not change my choice.
Whether UPR (B047) or CAR-T (B014) is better placed to be paired with GLP-1 in a later year, given the credit gaps for B014 (Eshhar and others) and the largely indirect clinical consequence of B047.
statement.conflict_note: No change. No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for the shortlisted ballots. My documented co-authorship with Thomas Perlmann concerns dopamine neuron work and involves no credited name on any shortlisted ballot, and I do not see a recusal issue. As chair I have tried to treat the round-1 exchange on its scientific content and not on support counts.
